2608.24361.title: Adaptive Influence Graphs for Failure Attribution in Multi-Agent Systems
2608.24361.paper_summary: Multi-agent LLM systems are increasingly deployed in real-world applications, where failures can be costly and difficult to localize. Despite growing efforts to automate failure attribution, diagnosing failed runs still largely relies on human engineers. Yet engineers rarely debug complex systems by reading raw logs end to end. Instead, observability tools organize traces around components, actions, and dependencies to support targeted navigation. We hypothesize that modern LLMs can benefit from the same paradigm. To test this hypothesis, we introduce Adaptive Influence Graphs (AIGs), a two-stage agentic framework that first transforms a failed trace into a structured graph and then navigates it to identify the critical error. Across multiple models, we show that richer trace representations consistently improve failure attribution, with adaptive graph construction and agent-directed traversal yielding the strongest results. AIGs establish a new state of the art on Who&When, the standard benchmark for multi-agent failure attribution. This affirms our hypothesis that attribution depends not only on the diagnosing model, but also on how the trace is represented and explored.
2608.24361.paper_summary_zh: 多代理 LLM 系統在現實世界的應用中越來越普遍，其中的故障可能代價高昂且難以定位。儘管自動化故障歸因的努力不斷增長，診斷失敗的運行仍然在很大程度上依賴於人類工程師。然而，工程師很少通過從頭到尾閱讀原始日誌來調試複雜系統。相反，可觀察性工具圍繞組件、行動和依賴性組織追蹤，以支持有針對性的導航。我們假設現代 LLM 可以從相同的範式中受益。為了驗證這一假設，我們引入了自適應影響圖 (AIGs)，這是一個兩階段的代理框架，首先將失敗的追蹤轉換為結構化圖，然後導航以識別關鍵錯誤。在多個模型中，我們顯示更豐富的追蹤表示一致地改善了故障歸因，自適應圖構建和代理導向的遍歷產生了最強的結果。AIGs 在 Who&When 上建立了新的最先進技術，這是多代理故障歸因的標準基準。這證實了我們的假設，即歸因不僅依賴於診斷模型，還取決於追蹤的表示和探索方式。
